title: Boundary finite-site evaluation and realization predicates
statement:
Let $C_T,C_Z$ be braided closed monoidal categories. For functors $s,G:C_T\to C_Z$, objects $W,V$, an isomorphism $h:G(W)\cong V$ and a morphism family $q_{M,N}:sM\otimes GN\to G(M\otimes N)$, define $\alpha_K$ by transposing $q_{K,[K,W]}$ followed by $G$ of evaluation and $h$. Define $\beta_L$ by transposing symmetry, $q_{[L,W],L}$, $G$ of symmetry and evaluation, then $h$. Define CompositeIdentity to be $s(\delta_K);\beta_{[K,W]}=\delta_{sK};[\alpha_K,V]$, with the canonical double-dual map [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, lem-weil-duality-pairing]. EtaleHypotheses says $s,G$ and the two dualities preserve their specified finite-Tor predicates and both etale double-dual maps are invertible.

For two such pairs of categories, functors and dualizing objects, define EvaluationTransport by the two alpha/beta comparison squares, transport of CompositeIdentity, preservation of invertibility on comparison images and invertibility on all pro-etale inputs. Specialize these definitions to the ordinary small etale and pro-etale derived categories, canonical comparison, exceptional functors, projection maps, q transposes and dualizing comparison isomorphisms [def-weil-boundary-q-maps, def-weil-boundary-q-pairing-transport, def-weil-boundary-composition-mate, def-weil-boundary-projection-comparison-data, def-weil-finite-duality-compatibility]. BasicConclusion packages the two finite-Tor comparison equivalences, preservation and reflection of Tor intervals, etale representatives, bounded-below Hom transport, Noetherianity and a natural-number dimension bound, canonical direct-image mate invertibility, exceptional counit normalization, and the ordinary projection comparison with invertible components. EvaluationConclusion packages dualizing-object membership, preservation, the normalized exceptional and duality comparisons and q naturality, together with EvaluationTransport. SiteConclusion is their conjunction at the actual operations. For a finite-field datum, a prime different from its characteristic, finite coefficient extension and positive quotient level, FiniteStatement is the implication from EtaleHypotheses to this SiteConclusion on the published finite-Tor predicates [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. EvaluationAt explicitly abbreviates the canonical evaluation specialization; SiteConclusion is BasicConclusion and EvaluationAt. Unfolding this factoring gives precisely the previously published formula. All existing signatures and meanings stay unchanged. BasicRemainder explicitly contains only the final six boundary clauses of the original BasicConclusion. BasicConclusion is the six finite-Tor comparison clauses followed by BasicRemainder. All canonical coefficient predicates remain exactly the original ones.
